findings.reason: the plan's own dispatch mechanism cannot reach the section without a followup carrying `/reckon-build the-crew-does-its-own-bookkeeping §29`.
findings.text: §29 is declared implementable but the followups section (plan.html:173) holds no article recommending it; every other open section s1–s28 has one, and a coordinator working the followup chain would never dispatch §29, so the section ships only if someone remembers it by hand

findings.reason: without it the node can implement a fix against a defect it never observed, which is exactly what the plan's opening paragraph says each section exists to prevent.
findings.text: §29's Deliverable begins at the mechanism, omitting the clause every other section carries ("First confirm that the defect still reproduces at main ... and record the reproduction in the manifest", the convention stated at plan.html:35); `_commit_state_write` already stages and commits once, so the defect could be closed or moved by a later commit, and a node without the reproduction step has no instruction to find out before writing code

findings.reason: the dispatch contract and §13's manifest check both require run-directory logs ending in `EXIT=`, so the omission costs a re-run at worst rather than changing what the section asks for.
findings.text: §29's done-when says only that the test files importing `reckon.ledger` add no failure and that ruff adds none, where every other section adds "Every log is under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command, and ends in `EXIT=`"; the node is left with no stated durable path for its base and head arms

findings.reason: a followup title is the dispatch text a coordinator copies, so it still advertises a goal its section no longer carries.
findings.text: `f-tcdiob-003` is titled "Build §3: a coordinator's review brief is used, and a resumed run's brief names its current head" and `f-tcdiob-007` (plan.html:206) is titled "Build §7: resume and reopen take a halted run, need no new write path, and report their own success", although §3 and §7 were retitled to their own single goal and the second half of each now belongs to §20 and §19; the same defect the author fixed for `f-tcdiob-016` by resolving and replacing it

response_events.note: An open followup, f-tcdiob-029, now names the build of §29.
§29's deliverable now begins by confirming the defect reproduces at main and recording it in the manifest.

rubric_items.done_when: pass — §29's three cases name what makes each pass, and its negative control removes the wait and states that the first case then raises, so the guard is falsifiable.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §29's done-when names no log location and no log discipline, unlike every other section, so the node's gate evidence has no stated durable path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §29's heading, symbols and write paths carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §29's deliverable drops the reproduction step that `_document` (plan.html:35) declares every section opens with, so the node may build a fix for a defect nobody confirmed still reproduces.
